sources.title: NGSS 4-LS1-1: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that function to support survival, growth, behavior, and reproduction
USDA Forest Service: Flower parts (Desert Gardeners)

legend.name: Stem and leaf
legend.meaning: Green: they make food from sunlight

legend.name: Petals
legend.meaning: Shown pink; petal colors vary by kind of flower

legend.name: Anthers
legend.meaning: Shown yellow, the color of much pollen

steps.title: Stem and leaves
steps.instruction: Trace the stem and its two leaves.

note.text: The stem holds the flower up. Inside, tubes carry water up from the roots. The leaves make food for the plant from sunlight.

steps.title: Sepals
steps.instruction: Trace the two small green sepals under the flower.

note.text: Sepals look like small leaves. Before the flower opened, they wrapped around the bud to protect it.
Colorful petals attract animals like bees. As they visit, they carry pollen from flower to flower.

steps.title: Stamens
steps.instruction: Trace the four stamens: each thin stalk and its anther on top.

note.text: Stamens make pollen. Each is a thin stalk, the filament, holding up an anther, where the pollen grows.

steps.title: Pistil
steps.instruction: Trace the pistil in the middle: the ovary, the style and the stigma on top.

note.text: The pistil's sticky top, the stigma, traps pollen. The style is the stalk that leads down to the ovary.

steps.title: Ovules
steps.instruction: Dab the three ovules inside the ovary.

note.text: After pollination, each ovule can become a seed, and the ovary around them grows into the fruit.
note.remember: Ovules become seeds; the ovary becomes the fruit.

steps.title: Color
steps.instruction: Color the flower. The pistil stays white so you can see the ovules.

steps.title: Label the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered part.

mistakes.Stigma: The stigma is on top of the pistil in the middle. This is on a stamen: it's an anther.

mistakes.Anther: Anthers are on the stamens around the edge. The sticky top in the middle is the stigma.

targets.role: Holds the ovules; becomes the fruit.

commonMistakes.Root: Roots are under the ground, holding the plant and taking in water.
commonMistakes.Seed: Seeds come later: the ovules inside the ovary become seeds after pollination.

steps.title: Explain
steps.question: How do a flower's parts help the plant make new plants?

options.text: Petals attract pollinators, which carry pollen to the stigma so seeds can form
options.feedback: Yes. Pollen from an anther must reach a stigma. Then ovules become seeds that grow into new plants.
The stem holds the flower up and carries water. Seeds form inside the ovary.
Sepals protect the bud. It's the ovary that grows into the fruit.

options.text: Petals soak up water for the seeds
options.feedback: Roots take in water. Petals help by attracting pollinators.
